claims.text: The target multi-principal-element alloy has low stacking-fault energy.
Cryo-rolling followed by annealing can generate a heterogeneous microstructure containing coarse and ultrafine grain regions.
Non-isothermal or partial-recrystallization annealing induces selective recrystallization rather than complete homogeneous recrystallization.
A subsequent aging treatment can form L12 nanoprecipitates in a Co-Cr-Ni-based alloy.
Cryo-rolling at 77 K to an 80–90% thickness reduction is an applicable processing condition for these alloy systems.
Annealing for one hour in the 800–900 °C range can retain or develop a heterogeneous microstructure after heavy rolling.
The proposed structure contains ultrafine grains of approximately 0.5–2 μm together with coarse grains.
Nanotwins may constitute the ultrafine structural component produced by the proposed treatment.
The heterogeneous structure can contain coherent L12 nanoprecipitates with very low matrix-precipitate lattice mismatch.
The proposed structure creates a multiscale gradient in hardness and strain compatibility.
Strain gradients between coarse and ultrafine regions generate back-stress or HDI strengthening.
Coherent nanoprecipitates contribute precipitation hardening.
Low matrix-precipitate lattice mismatch prevents premature interfacial decohesion.
The heterogeneous microstructure promotes dynamic strain hardening through geometrically necessary dislocation accumulation and possible dynamic twinning.
Dynamic strain hardening delays tensile necking.
The treated alloy can achieve a yield strength above 1.4 GPa.
The treated alloy can achieve uniform elongation above 13%.
The proposed treatment simultaneously outperforms standard homogeneous annealed counterparts in yield strength and tensile ductility.

Standard isothermal annealing at about 900 °C for one hour fully recrystallizes the same alloy into a homogeneous microstructure lacking the hierarchical grain structure and coherent precipitate distribution.
Annealing above 900 °C destroys the hierarchical or lamellar structure and produces inferior mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The intervention treats annealing at 800–900 °C for one hour as a partial/selective-recrystallization step, whereas the baseline states that 900 °C for one hour produces full recrystallization and a homogeneous structure. The fields do not specify another parameter that resolves these different outcomes.

The baseline attributes the homogeneous control to standard annealing, but the experiment does not clearly state whether Batch B receives the same prior cryo-rolling history as Batch A. Consequently, the control may differ in both rolling and annealing rather than only in the proposed thermal treatment.
